prompt:
**(a)** Express $\dfrac{1}{r(r+1)}$ in partial fractions. **[2]**

**(b)** Hence show that $\displaystyle\sum_{r=1}^{n}\frac{1}{r(r+1)}=\frac{n}{n+1}$. **[3]**
markscheme:
**(a)** $1\equiv A(r+1)+Br$: $r=0\Rightarrow A=1$, $r=-1\Rightarrow B=-1$, so $\dfrac1r-\dfrac1{r+1}$ **(M1)(A1)**

**(b)** $\left(1-\tfrac12\right)+\left(\tfrac12-\tfrac13\right)+\dots+\left(\tfrac1n-\tfrac1{n+1}\right)$ **(M1)**

All intermediate terms cancel **(R1)**, leaving $1-\dfrac{1}{n+1}=\dfrac{n}{n+1}$ **(A1)(AG)**
